plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in Sydney and Brisbane turn lavender-blue when this tree flowers. Clusters of trumpet-shaped blooms open on the tree's feathery canopy. They then drop to cover pavements and parked cars in a violet carpet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring in the Southern Hemisphere, from October to early December. Bloom is at its fullest in November.
plants.location: Sydney and Brisbane, eastern Australia. The tree is native to South America.
plants.funFact: The jacaranda comes from northwest Argentina and Bolivia. Australians have long joked that its flowering signals the start of university exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy evergreen shrub lights up the autumn garden when most other plants are fading. Its delicate, often lightly scented flowers range from single to loose, rose-like forms. Bees visit them on mild days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter, with flowers peaking from October through November in the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.location: Gardens in temperate regions such as Britain, the Pacific Northwest and the southeastern United States. The species is native to southern Japan.
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant. Its seeds are pressed to make a culinary and cosmetic oil in Japan.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: In its native Mexico, the poinsettia is a tall, open shrub, very different from the compact pot plants sold in shops. It carries fiery bracts that look like petals around tiny golden flower clusters.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter, with flowering from November to December. Short days trigger the color change.
plants.location: Mexico, its native range, and warm frost-free regions worldwide.
plants.funFact: The bright red parts are modified leaves called bracts. The real flowers are the small yellow cups, called cyathia, at the center.
